points.description: Step 1: mRNA leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore and travels through the cytoplasm to a ribosome (or enters the rough ER / ribosome attached to it). Both the exit and the arrival at the ribosome should be mentioned for full marks.

levels.says: Only one of the two ideas given (exits via nuclear pore OR goes to ribosome).

points.description: Step 2 (initiation): the ribosome reads mRNA bases in triplets called codons, starting at a START codon (AUG) in the P site; the first tRNA binds there.

levels.says: Mentions only codons read in triplets, or only the START codon, not both.

points.description: Step 3 (elongation): tRNA carrying the complementary anticodon recognizes and pairs with the mRNA codon (A-U, C-G); the amino acid on the tRNA is bonded (peptide bond) to the adjacent amino acid, and the ribosome moves on so a new tRNA/amino acid is added, building the chain.

levels.says: Mentions anticodon-codon pairing or amino acids being linked/added, but not both.

points.description: Step 4 (termination): amino acids continue to be added until a STOP codon is read (in the A site); the chain is released as a finished protein.

levels.says: Mentions chain continuing or ending without naming STOP codon, or only STOP codon with no release/ending.

rubric.notes: Award marks for four distinct steps in order, each described, not just listed. Equivalent wording is accepted; steps must follow the sequence from mRNA exit to termination. Naming a step without describing it earns at most half of that point's marks.
